title: Fail-closed temporal certificate extension for verified dynamic-top flux regime

depends_on.RM17: dynamic-top and explicit qtop=-36 raw solves are bit-identical

problem: The Reference temporal indicator currently rejects every non-EXPLICIT_FLUX top boundary before evaluating the defect, even when a dynamic-top provider is demonstrably state-independent and explicit-flux equivalent over the accepted trajectory.
operator_derivation: When all three path checks return the same FLUX value, the dynamic provider contributes zero state derivative to the temporal defect operator on the verified path. The existing explicit-flux operator, which contains no top-face stiffness, is therefore reused unchanged.
tests: Existing explicit fixed-flux temporal-indicator tests must remain bit-identical.
For the RM17 dynamic and explicit raw solve results, the temporal indicator with the same valid predecessor derivative must produce the same status, availability and head_inf_bound within 1e-12 cm.
The dynamic route must identify itself separately in diagnostics.
A dynamic provider switched to HEAD regime must remain unavailable.
A dynamic FLUX provider whose base/mid/candidate fluxes differ must remain unavailable.
Nonzero dynamic runoff or provider ponding must remain unavailable.
failure_rule: Do not modify the defect operator, temporal budget, predecessor history semantics, solver, retry policy or numerical tolerances to obtain a pass.
nonclaims: No precipitation, evaporation, snowmelt or runon certificate.
No general dynamic-top certificate beyond the fail-closed verified constant-flux envelope.
No three-model admission until RM18 is qualified and the unchanged RM14/RM13B physical case is rerun prospectively.
